important_caveats: The raw-moment Mahalanobis and zero-tilt tangent quantities are mechanism diagnostics, not substitutes for the exact I-projected weighted-Poisson action.
Full-TC is a historical optimizer from the old Stage-B reference geometry; D8 is optimized under the new endpoint-trained D5 reference and finite-resource screens.
Finite-law and exact-law comparisons use the same D5 reference. A persistent exact-law gap attributes the difference upstream of finite measurement noise.
The validation comparison is paired by the original D8 CRN trial index.
interpretation: Exact-population projected-law MMD: D8 is -29.51% relative to Full. If this is already strongly negative, the law advantage is not created by finite measurement noise.
I-projection improvement over raw D5 reference: D8=+0.0000e+00, Full=+0.0000e+00. A larger D8 improvement means its measurements pull the same D5 reference more strongly toward the external law.
D8-vs-Full finite-action reduction is -64.17% by ratio of means; negative means D8 is MORE expensive. Low action alone therefore does not imply better law fidelity.
Between-alpha target-moment sensitivity trace ratio D8/Full=10.352. Values >1 support the hypothesis that D8 measures the scientifically varying alpha direction more strongly.
Raw-reference standardized moment-mismatch ratio D8/Full=0.196. Values >1 mean D8 more clearly detects that the raw D5 reference is off-fiber relative to the external scientific law.
Zero-tilt dynamic-burden proxy ratio D8/Full=0.186. This is only an upstream diagnostic; the authoritative realization cost remains the weighted-Poisson action.
purpose: Explain why the D8 sensor has much better law fidelity than historical Full-TC while Full-TC has lower realization action under the D5 endpoint-trained reference.
